one_month_reasoning: Q3 earnings fall outside the window: CoreWeave reported Q2 on Aug 11 and Q3 is expected roughly Nov 5-16, with no date announced yet. Events inside the window: (1) the 35M-share Equity Distribution Agreement (ATM plus collared forwards, 8-K 9/17) can start about 30 days after the 9/17 convert purchase agreement, so from roughly Oct 17. That is up to ~6% potential supply, a mild overhang. (2) Ongoing 10b5-1 insider selling: seven Form 144s were filed 9/29-9/30 and the CEO sold 200k shares at $86.82 on 9/22. A mild negative. (3) Hyperscaler and Meta Q3 earnings in late October, where AI capex commentary moves neocloud stocks in either direction. (4) Convert hedge flows after the $4.2B 2033 notes (conversion price $97.85), which tend to damp upside near $98. No company-specific binary event, so I keep a near-symmetric lognormal on log price with a median of ~$87.6 (a slight tilt below $88.57 for the ATM and insider supply) and monthly sigma ~25%, close to the 93%/3.5 rule of thumb.

fair_value.method: Equal-weight blend of a 12-month-forward DCF ($74: WACC 11%, terminal growth 3%, revenue $26B in 2027 rising to $73B by 2035, adj. EBITDA margin ~60% fading to 56%, capex 2.5x incremental revenue, 8-year GPU economic life, net debt $37B, 605M shares) and an EV/EBITDA exit ($96: 6.0x NTM Oct-2027 adj. EBITDA of $19.7B, less $58.7B net debt, 622M shares). Blend = $85, about at the current price.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FCFF 2026-2035 + Gordon terminal; WACC 11.0% (CoE 14.0%, after-tax Kd 6.7%, 58/42 E/D); g 3%; revenue 12.8/26/38/48/56/62/66/69/71/73 $B; adj. EBITDA 59-60% fading to 56%, less SBC 5%->3%; capex = 2.5x next-year revenue increment + replacement at 85% of cost after 8 years (2026 capex $37B); D&A 6-yr straight line; tax 21% after NOLs. EV $76.6B (PV explicit $19.5B + PV TV $57.1B), less $37B net debt = $39.6B equity / 605M = $65 today, x1.14 roll-forward = ~$74. Very sensitive: k 2.3-2.7 and life 7-8 years give -$4 to $91 a share today; WACC +/-50bp moves it ~+/-$11.

bear.story: AI-capex digestion or a top-customer wobble (Customer A 36% and B 26% of Q2 revenue) meets ~$60B of net debt. The cost of funding rises (unsecured notes already at 9-9.75%) and recontracting prices for Hopper roll-offs soften, so the market reprices the 6-year depreciation and 'second contract' risk. EV/EBITDA compresses to ~4.5x on ~$17B EBITDA and the leverage roughly halves the equity.

base.story: Execution is broadly on guidance: FY26 revenue ~$12.8B, adj. op margin reaches low teens in Q4, exit-2027 run-rate approaches $30B, and backlog grows past $130B including the >$25B early-Q3 adds. Each dollar of growth is offset by debt and dilution from the ATM and converts, so the multiple stays ~6x NTM EBITDA and the stock ends near fair value of ~$85-90.

bull.story: Pricing power persists: the July ~25% list increase, very high short-dated contract pricing, and A100/H200 renewals at premiums push stabilized margins toward management's 25-30% long-term target. Financing costs keep falling (investment-grade DDTLs) and inference demand broadens. The multiple re-rates to ~8x on ~$21B forward EBITDA, and the shares retest the 52-week high near $153 and go beyond.

thesis_break_reason: A sustained move below ~$55 (under the July 2026 low of $60.55 and about 37% below today) would most likely mean the market is pricing a fundamental problem rather than volatility: a top-customer contract cut or delay, a failed or punitive financing (DDTL or high-yield market shut, much wider spreads), a guidance cut on delivery delays, or evidence that renewal pricing for older GPUs is collapsing. At ~$55 the equity is only ~$34B against roughly $40B of net debt now and ~$60B next year, so the equity cushion over the asset-backed debt becomes thin.

reasoning: Primary documents set the base. Q2'26 revenue was $2.575B (+112% YoY) with adj. EBITDA margin 59% and adj. op margin 5%. Net loss was $626M on $640M of interest. RPO is $103.7B (41% inside 24 months), and over $25B was added in early Q3. FY26 guidance was raised to revenue $12.4-13.2B, adj. op income $0.96-1.15B and capex $35-39B, with exit-2026 run-rate $18.5-19.5B. The Q4'25 call set exit-2027 run-rate >$30B and a 25-30% long-term margin target. The balance sheet is the swing factor: $35.6B of debt at 6/30 plus August draws and the $4.2B 2.875% 2033 converts, and the 8-K of 9/17 shows a 35M-share ATM. In the 10-Q, in-service gross PP&E of ~$40.7B against $10.3B of annualized revenue implies ~3.5x capex intensity on a ramping base. That intensity, set against a 6-year book life, decides whether this business earns its 11% WACC. My DCF credits recent price increases (k 2.5x) and the A100/H200 recontracting evidence (8-year economic life) and gets ~$65 today, ~$74 in 12 months. Being honest about sensitivity: small changes in k or life move it from below zero to ~$90. An EV/EBITDA cross-check using CRWV's own current ~6.4x NTM multiple, applied at 6.0x a year out after a projected ~$22B rise in net debt, gives ~$96. The 50/50 blend is $85, close to the $88.57 spot. So I see no strong fundamental edge and use a wide, roughly fair-valued distribution: median ~$80 and lognormal sigma ~0.70 (below 84-93% realized, since vol typically compresses as a name matures, but still very wide), which puts the mean near $100, consistent with a ~14% cost of equity. The median sits below spot because of the volatility drag and the dilution and leverage overhang. Scenario check: bear $42 (28%) / base $88 (50%) / bull $165 (22%) gives a mean of ~$92. Consensus (41 analysts, $141.58 average target, 2027 EPS -$1.81) was treated as evidence of sell-side optimism, not as an anchor. Research limits: Twelve Data estimates and statistics endpoints and Alpha Vantage were unavailable (plan or rate limits), so consensus figures come from public aggregator pages.
